questions.question: How can you tell if the whole of an object is floating on water?
options: If some of its volume is visible above the surface of the water.
If the entire object is completely submerged.
If it sinks all the way to the bottom.
If it dissolves completely in the water.

questions.question: A wooden block floats in a shallow tray of water. If we move it to a very deep swimming pool filled with the same water, how does its ability to float change?
options: It floats better because there is more space.
It does not float as well because the depth has increased.
It floats exactly the same because floating does not depend on the depth of the liquid.
It sinks because deeper water exerts less upward force.

questions.question: Under what condition will an object float in water?
options: If its shape can push its own mass of water out of the way without going under.
Only if its mass is greater than 100 kilograms.
If its shape allows it to absorb all the water around it.
Only if it is completely flat and has no volume.

questions.question: Approximately how much upward force is required to lift a 1 kg object on Earth?
options: 1 N

questions.question: What force does a 1 kg mass exert downwards when resting on a table on Earth?
options: About 1 N
About 5 N
About 10 N
About 100 N

questions.question: Which equation is used to calculate gravitational force (weight, W) using mass (m) and gravitational field strength (g)?
options: W = m x g
W = m / g
W = g / m
W = m + g

questions.question: If a spring has a regular elastic behavior, what happens to its extension for each equal-sized increase in force applied?
options: The extension increases by a larger amount each time.
The extension increases by a smaller amount each time.
The extension increases by the same amount each time.
The extension remains completely zero.

questions.question: Why is a spring described as being elastic?
options: It permanently changes its shape after a small pull.
It returns to its original length when a force is removed.
It can only be stretched once before snapping.
It becomes warmer when a force is applied to it.

questions.question: What is a useful function of a lever regarding force?
options: Levers can multiply a small force into a larger force.
Levers always reduce the force to zero.
Levers can destroy force completely.
Levers can only work without any force.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines pressure?
options: It is a measure of the total weight of an object.
It is a measure of how concentrated a force is.
It is the speed at which an object is pushed.
It is the energy stored inside a stretched material.

questions.question: How is pressure calculated?
options: Pressure = force x area
Pressure = force / area
Pressure = area / force
Pressure = force + area

questions.question: What is another name for the unit of pressure 'newtons per square metre' (N/m2)?
options: The joule (J)
The watt (W)
The pascal (Pa)
The newton (N)

questions.question: Why does pressure in a liquid increase as you go deeper?
options: Because the liquid gets warmer at the bottom.
Because there is more liquid pushing down from above.
Because the density of the liquid decreases.
Because the liquid particles stop moving.

questions.question: Why does atmospheric pressure decrease as you climb a high mountain?
options: Because there is less air pushing down from above.
Because the gravity of the Earth increases with height.
Because the air temperature is always constant.
Because the speed of wind decreases.

questions.question: What happens to a horizontal support beam as you place a bigger mass on it?
options: The beam bends more.
The beam completely straightens out.
The beam's mass decreases.
The beam does not change its shape at all.

questions.question: How does the force a beam pushes back with change as it bends more?
options: The force it pushes back with decreases.
The force it pushes back with increases.
The force it pushes back with becomes zero.
The force it pushes back with remains constant.

questions.question: When an object squashes the particles in a floor closer together, what is the effect on the force they push back with?
options: They push back with a greater force.
They stop pushing back entirely.
They push back with a smaller force.
The upward force remains completely unchanged.

questions.question: How is the moment of a force calculated?
options: Moment = force / perpendicular distance from the pivot
Moment = force x perpendicular distance from the pivot
Moment = perpendicular distance / force
Moment = force + perpendicular distance from the pivot
